AFDJAX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Jacksonville FL
722 AM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

For the latest NE FL and SE GA Daily Key Messages please visit:
https:/www.weather.gov/media/jax/briefings/nws-jax-briefing.pdf

- Scattered to Numerous Afternoon & Evening TStorms Each Day
  through the Weekend and Early Next Week. Primary Concern will
  be Lightning and Heavy Downpours resulting in Localized
  Flooding. 

- Moderate Rip Current Risk Continues at All Area Beaches

&&

.NEAR TERM /THROUGH TONIGHT/...
Highlights through Tonight:

- Waves of heavy downpours may lead to localized minor flooding this 
afternoon

Skies have trended mostly clear with convection persisting well 
offshore this morning. In the scope of the broader weather pattern, 
there will be on subtle changes today. The primary change will be a 
strengthening southwesterly steering flow owing to the sharpening of 
mean layer troughing across the Appalachians and into the Deep 
South. A broader blanket of deep moisture, sourced from the Gulf, 
will channeled south of a decaying frontal zone situated across 
central GA. This will keep "high grade" (near the 90th percentile) 
across NE FL and SE GA today, fueling waves of scattered to numerous 
showers and convection this morning and afternoon. This pattern will 
favor an initial late morning bout of scattered thunderstorms moving 
from the Big Bend northeastward as morning heating erodes the "cap" 
by 10-11 AM. That activity is expected to reach the Atlantic coast 
around 1-3 PM followed by additional waves through the afternoon.  

Given the increase in the offshore steering winds and potential for 
earlier showers and thunderstorms, the Atlantic sea breeze may not 
be able to establish or push inland this afternoon. Poor lapse rates 
aloft and the Atlantic sea breeze being potentially pinned over the 
coastal waters will minimize the potential of stronger thunderstorm 
this afternoon. The main focus with storms will be the potential for 
waves of heavy downpours over areas that have already received a few 
inches during the last few days. 

Similar to last few evenings, a decline in thunderstorm coverage 
will occur with the loss of heating with minimal, if any, leftover 
shower activity after 10 PM. There will be another prefrontal 
boundary approaching Friday morning and this may help initiate 
predawn showers along the Big Bend which could push toward portions 
of the lower Suwannee Valley through sunrise.

Near normal afternoon temperatures are expected today, with highs 
again in the low 90s and peak heat index in the upper 90s and lower 
100s. Temperatures tonight will be similar to low this morning, 
generally in the low 70s inland and mid 70s at the coast.

&&

.SHORT TERM /FRIDAY THROUGH SATURDAY NIGHT/...
Main Highlights This Period: ( Friday through Saturday night )

- Strong storms are expected each day, with a few severe storms 
possible

Surface high pressure will be centered to the northeast this period, 
with a frontal zone nearly stationary across GA. The region will 
also be under a weak upper trough. 

A combination of ample moisture, instability under upper trough, 
frontal convergence, diurnal instability and sea breeze interactions 
will result in above average coverage of mainly afternoon and 
evening showers and thunderstorms. A few strong to severe 
thunderstorms will be possible each day. 

Temperatures will trend a little above average this period.

&&

.LONG TERM /SUNDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Main Highlights This Period: ( Sunday through Wednesday )

- A few strong to severe thunderstorms possible each afternoon and 
evening

Surface high pressure will remain centered to the northeast of the 
region this period, while the persistent frontal zone over southern 
GA gradually dissipates. A ridge of high pressure will build 
overhead this period. 

Daily convection will largely be driven by diurnal instability this 
period. The upper high will help to limit activity somewhat, but a 
few strong to severe storms can not be ruled out each afternoon.

Temperatures will trend near seasonal levels this period.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z THURSDAY THROUGH 12Z FRIDAY/...
Southwesterly flow will bring waves of showers during the late 
morning, then scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon. 
Thunderstorms will bring the potential for flight category 
reductions, primarily due to visibility for short durations during 
the afternoon hours (18-00z) with activity generally, moving 
eastward off the coast or decreasing in strength and coverage after 
00z. For now, maintained PROB30s for most of the TAF sites, but
TEMPOs may be necessary to add later on. VFR conditions with 
leftover cloud debris is expected through the evening with light
southerly winds.

&&

.MARINE...

A stalled front to the north will be replaced by another front 
which is also expected to stall just to the north of the local 
waters this weekend. Offshore winds will prevail through Friday 
night, then shift onshore over the weekend as high pressure 
builds to the north over the weekend, then to the northeast and 
into the western Atlantic early next week. Afternoon 
thunderstorms remain possible today and Friday due the 
prevailing offshore winds, followed by decreasing chances this 
weekend into next week as onshore flow develops.

Rip Currents: A very low end Moderate Risk of rip currents is 
expected this afternoon after the sea breeze develops. Similar 
expectation on Friday. Prevailing winds turn onshore this weekend, 
leading to a more solid Moderate risk.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...

High pressure will be located to the northeast throughout this 
period. A frontal zone will be nearly stationary over southern GA 
through Sunday. Daily rounds of showers and thunderstorms each day, 
mainly in the afternoon and evening hours. 

Fog Potential: Significant fog is unlikely over the next several 
days. Gusty and erratic winds can be expected in and near 
thunderstorms.

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
AMG  92  72  91  71 /  60  50  80  40 
SSI  89  76  89  76 /  50  30  50  60 
JAX  91  72  91  72 /  50  20  70  40 
SGJ  91  74  90  74 /  50  20  60  40 
GNV  90  72  89  72 /  60  20  50  20 
OCF  90  72  90  72 /  60  10  60  30 

&&

.JAX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
FL...None.
GA...None.
MARINE...None.

&&
